newsitem.title: FINLAND: SALOMON SEES STILL UPSIDE IN MERITA.
newsitem.headline: SALOMON SEES STILL UPSIDE IN MERITA.

text.p: Salomon Brothers said there was still upside in Finnish Merita Bank's shares as there was scope for profitability to rise further in 1997 and 1998.

"Some of this forecast improvement in profitability is already in the price; in our view there is still further upside," Salomon Brothers said in a Nordic banking overview dated November 14, and maintained its "buy" recommendation.
Merita's vote strong A share closed at 13.90 markka on November 14, and its B share closed at 15.00 markka.
On Friday at 1200/1000 GMT, the A share traded at 14.30 markka, down 0.10 on Thursday's close, and Merita B was unchanged at 15.80 markka.
Merita's earnings per share are expected to rise to 0.80 markka in 1996 and to 1.40 markka in 1997 from 0.51 markka in 1995, Salomon Brothers said.
It did not give any EPS estimate for 1998.

Salomon said it expects Merita to pay a 0.20 markka dividend on A shares for 1996 and 0.40 markka for 1997. It did not give a dividend estimate for the preferential B share, which carries right to dividend before A shares.
Merita's January-September report showed a 0.98 markka earnings per share, up from 0.61 markka in the first nine months of 1995.
